data.title: Gen İlaç boosts control of Neo Auvra with majority stake in digital health firm
data.description:
Gen Ilac ve Saglik Urunleri Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. ( (TR:GENIL) ) has shared an announcement.

Gen İlaç ve Sağlık Ürünleri Sanayi ve Ticaret A.Ş. has increased its stake in Neo Auvra Dijital Sağlık ve Biyonik Teknolojileri ve Hizmetleri Sanayi ve Ticaret A.Ş. by acquiring an additional 41.79% of the company’s share capital, raising its ownership from 35.15% to 76.94%. This move consolidates Gen İlaç’s control over Neo Auvra, signaling a stronger commitment to digital health and bionic technologies and potentially enhancing its strategic influence, governance, and long-term positioning in advanced healthcare solutions.

Following the share transfer, changes in Neo Auvra’s Board of Directors were registered and announced in the Turkish Trade Registry Gazette, formalizing the new ownership and governance structure. The transaction underscores Gen İlaç’s effort to deepen integration with its digital health subsidiary, which may have implications for operational synergies, innovation capability, and future expansion in technology-driven medical services.

data.title: Anton Oilfield Gains Iraq Crude Sales Role, Expands Full-Chain Services
data.description:
The latest update is out from Anton Oilfield Services Group ( (HK:3337) ).

Anton Oilfield Services Group has secured approval from Iraq’s Ministry of Oil to enter a long-term cooperation with the State Oil Marketing Company, gaining crude oil sales qualification and becoming a designated partner for crude oil export sales. The group obtained lifting rights for self-operated oilfields of Iraq’s national oil company and general long-term sales cooperation status, positioning it as a lifting and settlement service provider that links crude oil sales with service providers and buyers.

Under the agreement, Anton will coordinate lifting arrangements, facilitate resource monetisation and support settlement needs across Iraq’s oil and gas ecosystem, while helping SOMO expand its market share. The new crude-linked settlement channel is described as an innovative business model that extends Anton’s service chain into oil and gas commercialisation support, strengthens ties with Iraqi authorities and enhances the company’s resilience, making it the only Chinese independent energy firm in Iraq with combined capabilities in technical services, resource development and crude oil sales.

data.title: Sunshine Oilsands to Issue Discounted Shares to Settle Debt
data.description:
Sunshine Oilsands ( (HK:2012) ) has shared an update.

Sunshine Oilsands has agreed to issue new shares under its existing general mandate to settle outstanding debts owed to certain creditors, converting liabilities into equity. The shares will be issued at HK$0.171, a discount to recent market prices, and will account for about 13.85% of current share capital, or 12.16% of the enlarged capital base once the transaction closes.

The issuance, which does not require additional shareholder approval, is intended to strengthen the company’s balance sheet by reducing debt obligations but will dilute existing shareholders’ stakes. Completion remains subject to conditions in the settlement agreement, and the company has warned investors to exercise caution, underscoring some execution risk and potential volatility around the stock as the deal proceeds.

data.title: China Environmental Technology Reaches Settlement Over Disputed Convertible Bonds
data.description:
China Environmental Technology Holdings Limited ( (HK:0646) ) has shared an announcement.

China Environmental Technology Holdings has settled a long-running dispute over its 2021 convertible bonds by signing a Deed of Settlement with creditor Sure Fast. The agreement follows prior court rulings affirming the validity and enforceability of the bond-related agreements, bringing greater clarity to the company’s financial obligations.

Under the Deed, the company will pay a final settlement sum of US$11.29 million plus interest in three instalments through the end of 2027. In return, Sure Fast has agreed not to pursue winding-up petitions, new legal actions, or enforcement of the Hong Kong High Court judgment, unless the company defaults, reducing immediate legal and insolvency risks for shareholders and creditors.

data.title: Agricultural Bank of China Seeks Fresh Share Issuance Mandate to Bolster Capital
data.description:
Agricultural Bank of China ( (HK:1288) ) just unveiled an update.

Agricultural Bank of China has proposed a new general mandate allowing its board to issue up to 15% of its existing A and H share capital, aiming to support steady business development, enhance long-term capital management, and increase flexibility in capital raising. The mandate, subject to shareholder approval at an extraordinary shareholders’ meeting, would enable the bank to issue up to about 47.9 billion A shares and 4.6 billion H shares, with pricing linked to the recent average trading price and authority to adjust registered capital and amend its articles accordingly.

Under this general mandate, the bank has drawn up an A share issuance plan to place new shares with specified investors, after confirming it meets regulatory requirements under Chinese company and securities laws. The proposed issuance, together with related subscription agreements involving key state-linked shareholders, is positioned to strengthen the bank’s capital base and could reinforce its competitive standing in China’s banking sector, though it may also dilute existing shareholders’ stakes depending on the final issuance size and terms.

data.title: Gamivo S.A. Named in California Class-Action Lawsuit Over GAMIVO.com Fees
data.description:
Gamivo SA ( (PL:GMV) ) has provided an update.

Gamivo S.A. has disclosed that it has been named, alongside GAMIVO.com Limited, in legal proceedings initiated in the Superior Court of California by an individual seeking class-action status. The lawsuit challenges how certain fees and services are presented and charged during the purchase process on the GAMIVO.com platform, though the plaintiff has not specified the value of the claims.

The company stresses that Gamivo S.A. is not the operator of the GAMIVO.com platform nor the entity processing consumer transactions, asserting that GAMIVO.com Limited manages sales, payments and order fulfillment. Management is disputing the legitimacy of the claims against the Polish parent, is working with legal advisors to assess its defense, and says it is currently unable to estimate any potential financial impact, with further updates to follow in line with disclosure rules.
